ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $ \triangle ABC$, $\angle ACB=90^\circ$. $BD=AB$ is taken on the extension line of $BC$, and $AD$ is connected. A perpendicular $BE\perp AD$ is drawn from point $B$ to point $E$, intersecting $AC$ at point $F$. $DF$ is connected. Point $P$ is a moving point on the ray $BE$. If $AC=9$ and $BC=12$, what is the length of $BP$ when $\triangle APB$ is similar to $\triangle AFD$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Connect AP. \\
In $\triangle ACB$, $\angle ACB=90^\circ$, $AC=9$, $BC=12$, \\
$\therefore AB=\sqrt{AC^{2}+BC^{2}}=\sqrt{9^{2}+12^{2}}=15$, \\
$\therefore BD=BA=15$, $CD=BD-BC=15-12=3$, \\
$\therefore AD=\sqrt{CD^{2}+AC^{2}}=\sqrt{3^{2}+9^{2}}=3\sqrt{10}$, \\
$\therefore BE\perp AD$, \\
$\therefore AE=ED$, \\
$\therefore FA=FD$, \\
Let $FA=FD=x$, then we have $x^{2}=(9-x)^{2}+3^{2}$, \\
$\therefore x=5$, \\
$\therefore FA=FD=5$, \\
Because $\angle AEF=\angle FCB=90^\circ$, $\angle AFE=\angle CFB$, \\
$\therefore \angle EAF=\angle ABP$, \\
When $\triangle APB \sim \triangle AFD$, $\frac{BP}{DF}=\frac{AB}{AD}$, \\
$\therefore \frac{BP}{5}=\frac{15}{3\sqrt{10}}$, \\
$\therefore BP=\frac{5\sqrt{10}}{2}$. \\
When $\triangle AFD \sim \triangle PAB$, $\frac{AD}{BP}=\frac{DF}{AB}$, \\
$\therefore \frac{3\sqrt{10}}{BP}=\frac{5}{15}$, \\
$\therefore BP=9\sqrt{10}$. \\
In conclusion, the length of $BP$ is $\boxed{\frac{5\sqrt{10}}{2}}$ or $\boxed{9\sqrt{10}}$.

method.method_draft: Use an analytic-coordinate route. From the figure choose coordinates aligned with the visible right angle and horizontal base: set C=(0,0), A=(0,9), B=(12,0). From the text AB=15, so because D lies on the extension of BC with BD=AB, take D=(-3,0). Then AD has slope 3, so BE, perpendicular to AD through B, has slope -1/3 and equation y=4-x/3. Its intersection with AC, the vertical line x=0, is F=(0,4). Therefore AF=5, DF=sqrt(3^2+4^2)=5, and AD=3sqrt(10). Parameterize P on ray BE by its distance t=BP: using the unit direction from B along BE, P=(12-3t/sqrt(10), t/sqrt(10)). Then AP^2=(12-3t/sqrt(10))^2+(t/sqrt(10)-9)^2=t^2-9sqrt(10)t+225. Triangle AFD has side lengths 5,5,3sqrt(10), while triangle APB has side lengths AP, t, 15. Compare possible side correspondences: if AB=15 corresponds to AD=3sqrt(10), the scale is sqrt(10)/2 and t must equal 5sqrt(10)/2, which also satisfies the AP formula. If AB=15 corresponds to one of the equal sides 5, the scale is 3; the feasible placement on ray BE gives t=9sqrt(10) and AP=15. Thus BP is 5sqrt(10)/2 or 9sqrt(10).

raw_record.original_question: In $\triangle ABC$, $\angle ACB=90^\circ$. Point $D$ lies on the extension of $BC$ such that $BD=AB$, and $AD$ is connected. From point $B$, draw $BE\perp AD$, intersecting $AC$ at point $F$. Connect $DF$. Point $P$ is a moving point on ray $BE$. If $AC=9$ and $BC=12$, what is the length of $BP$ when $\triangle APB$ is similar to $\triangle AFD$?
raw_record.answer: Solution: Connect $AP$. In $\triangle ACB$, $\angle ACB=90^\circ$, $AC=9$, $BC=12$, so $AB=\sqrt{AC^{2}+BC^{2}}=\sqrt{9^{2}+12^{2}}=15$. Therefore $BD=BA=15$, and $CD=BD-BC=15-12=3$. Hence $AD=\sqrt{CD^{2}+AC^{2}}=\sqrt{3^{2}+9^{2}}=3\sqrt{10}$. Since $BE\perp AD$, we get $AE=ED$, so $FA=FD$. Let $FA=FD=x$, then $x^{2}=(9-x)^{2}+3^{2}$, giving $x=5$. Thus $FA=FD=5$. When $\triangle APB \sim \triangle AFD$, $\frac{BP}{DF}=\frac{AB}{AD}$, so $\frac{BP}{5}=\frac{15}{3\sqrt{10}}$, hence $BP=\frac{5\sqrt{10}}{2}$. When $\triangle AFD \sim \triangle PAB$, $\frac{AD}{BP}=\frac{DF}{AB}$, so $\frac{3\sqrt{10}}{BP}=\frac{5}{15}$, hence $BP=9\sqrt{10}$. Therefore, $BP=\frac{5\sqrt{10}}{2}$ or $9\sqrt{10}$.
raw_record.final_cot: Image description: In the figure A is directly above C, AC is vertical, D, C, B are on the same horizontal line and C is between D and B; AD is the left oblique side, AB is the right oblique side; BE drawn from B is perpendicular to AD and intersects AC at F, E is on AD; DF has been connected; P is on the ray from B along the direction of BE. Reasoning: In right triangle ABC, AC=9, BC=12, so AB=√(9^2+12^2)=15. Also BD=AB=15, and BC=12, so CD=BD-BC=3. Thus in right triangle ACD, AD=√(AC^2+CD^2)=√(9^2+3^2)=3√10. Because BA=BD, and BE passes through B and is perpendicular to AD, BE is the perpendicular bisector of AD, therefore F on it satisfies FA=FD. Let FA=FD=x, then F is on AC, CF=9-x; in right triangle DCF, x^2=(9-x)^2+3^2, solving gives x=5, so DF=5. Now consider the feasible corresponding relationships for triangle APB and triangle AFD to be similar. First: AB corresponds to AD, BP corresponds to DF, then BP/5=15/(3√10), obtaining BP=5√10/2. Second: BP corresponds to AD, AB corresponds to DF, then (3√10)/BP=5/15, obtaining BP=9√10. Therefore BP has two possible values.
